questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Family and friends

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I also were in contact with the one who was responsible for the erasmus-student, and she was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Needed some help from the one who was responsible for the erasmus-student, she helped me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy since my brother already lived there. It is called Anker Studentbolig

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find and apply for housing as soon as possible, they will be rented out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its very central and close to both the campus and central station.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to log into a webside (StudentWeb) through the UiO webside, and chose and apply for the classes you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got some help from the one who was responsible for the erasmus-student. Don´t know if there were any other help that was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes i applied for, very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the one who was responsible for the erasmus-student for help if you need help, he or she is very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was expected, and there were different requirements for the BA and MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The had much more task solutions and active students. They also download lectures online, and upload material from lectures which makes it very easy to study for the exam

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
5550 Helserett
5590 Diskriminerings- og likestillingsrett
5280 Internasjonal Privatrett

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since I am norwegian I was taking norwegian classes. Both Helserett and Diskriminerings- og likestillingsrett as these were very interesting and easy to follow the lectures, a lot of activities in the lectures aswell.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, i have lived in Norway before.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: None, I knew the prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Download the SiO app, it is 400+ activities, both non-academic and academic.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything, it is always something going on. I'm sure everyone will find something they like.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the buddy week, it is socializing and fun. You also get to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
SiO have a eventcalender where you can find all activities.
https://www.sio.no/eventkalender
, it´s also in english. You can also use this webside
https://www.sio.no/en
to find information about housing, health, spots, food and beverage and associations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy because I'm Norwegian

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be curious and open and the norwegians likes partying

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Nature and Scenery
Outdoor Lifestyle

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Join the buddy week
- Download the SiO app and use the webside. 
- Attend the lectures

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join Facebook-groups and sides. I will recommend if you understand norwegian that you join (law-students) the group Rettsvitenskap UiO, where you can find job applications, both academic and social activities etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To have everything online aswell as the lecture on campus. New friends and memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It took me a while to figure out where to find social activities. And it was difficult to find places on campus, for example reading places for exams

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
